1.why: Four unrelated relations (contrast, cause, hedge, parallel); with the sentences hidden nothing rules any out.

2.why: Causal, inferential, parallel and concessive are all live without the text.

3.why: Exemplification, contrast, simultaneity and restatement are mutually exclusive but all possible blind.

4.why: Concession, restatement, simultaneity and substitution are distinct and none is self-defeating on its own.

5.why: No two options mean the same thing, so no option can be argued illegal without the sentences.

6.why: Contrast, restatement, parallel and simultaneity all remain available blind.

7.why: The stem asks to contrast the two studies' FINDINGS: D is the only option that states both findings and opposes them; A contrasts publication and samples, C contrasts sample sizes (method, not finding), B reports one study only.

8.why: Result, comparison, concession and anteriority are distinct relations, none eliminable from the option set.

9.why: Stem asks why it MATTERS to a general reader: A and C only describe the old constraint and the motivation, so they answer a different question; D states the human consequence and B merely restates the mechanism, leaving D the only one framed as significance.

10.why: 'Thus' and 'For this reason' are interchangeable causal connectives, so neither can be uniquely correct and both fall; the pick between restatement and contrast is a coin flip.

11.why: Stem asks for a single conclusion supported by ALL THREE studies; A, C and D each report one study, so only B is a generalization across them.

12.why: Stem asks for a CAUTIOUS generalization a skeptic would accept: A ('can be expected to hold across most job types') and D ('beyond reasonable dispute for any job') overreach, B is a dismissal rather than a generalization, leaving only the hedged C.

13.why: Contrast, consequence-chain, parallel and intensification are all live blind.

14.why: Restatement, simultaneity, result and concession are distinct; nothing in the set self-eliminates.

15.why: Example, parallel, contrast and result are mutually exclusive but all possible without the text.

16.why: Sequence-closing, parallel, concession and consequence all remain legal blind.

17.why: 'At the same time' can be temporal as well as concessive, so it does not collapse into 'On the other hand'; all four stay legal.

18.why: Intensification, contrast, example and temporal are distinct relations, none eliminable.

19.why: Sequence, concession, parallel and summary are all available without the sentences.

20.why: Result, intensification, parallel and concession are distinct; no option is illegal on its face.

21.why: Simultaneity, restatement, substitution and conditional-consequence are all live blind.

22.why: Stem asks to emphasize a DIFFERENCE in distance between the two species: A asserts similarity, C and D each give one species' distance with nothing to compare it to, so only B states both figures in a contrastive frame.

23.why: Stem names two things that must both appear - self-rated alertness and measured performance: C and D supply neither, A supplies only performance, so only B contains the disconnect.

24.why: Simultaneity, concession, consequence and summary are distinct and all possible without the text.
